text:
jess-support: Customer 'LanternLabs' (dedicated pool eu-west-2) reporting sudden p95 token latency jumps and intermittent 429s starting ~08:15 UTC. They've got 4 nodes with MIG 1g.10gb partitions. Customer saw a ~3x p95 and a few evictions. Can SRE help triage?

kevin-sre: Can you paste the tenant/job ids + the node ids? Also any recent autoscale events?

jess-support: tenant=lantern-prod-17, job=jl-842, nodes=[eu2-node-17, eu2-node-21, eu2-node-44, eu2-node-88]. Autoscale: bumped from 3->4 at 08:12 after a CPU warmup spike. No config changes.

anya-ml: Noticed their request traces show repeated KV cache misses around the spike window. Could be slice packing fragmentation causing more GPU work per token.

sophie-eng-runtime: @kevin-sre tagging you — I pulled short diagnostics from eu2-node-44. Putting raw snippets below.

sophie-eng-runtime: ```
# nvidia-smi topo -m
GPU0    GPU1    GPU2    GPU3
... (fabric shows uneven links, small flaps)

# /opt/redwood/bin/migctl status
node: eu2-node-44
partitions: 1g.10gb x3, leftover 2g.20gb x1
slice-util: GPU0 72% GPU1 68% GPU2 91% GPU3 28%

# dmesg | tail -n 20
[08:12:14] MIG vGPU reset on GPU2
[08:12:17] kernel: nvlink error: retrain event
```

jess-support: Customer also attached a short trace showing many small fanout requests at same time (tiny prompts). They routined to dedicated slot.

kevin-sre: Hmm GPU2 hot. The MIG reset is suspicious — could be NVML/driver-level glitch causing eviction handshake that cascades to other slices. Did we see throttling metrics from the runtime?

infra-bot: autoscaler: scale_up job jl-842 triggered at 08:12 (reason: queue_depth > 80%), new node eu2-node-44 added at 08:14.

sophie-eng-runtime: Runtime metrics (sample):
```
model: redwood-13b-v1
node: eu2-node-44
p50: 80ms p95: 1.2s p99: 2.8s
device_sm_util: 92%
requests_inflight: bursty tiny requests -> high kernel launch churn
```

anya-ml: That kernel churn + high SM util on a single MIG slice explains tail. If MIG partitions are unevenly packed we get cross-slice contention for L2/L3 and memory bandwidth.

kevin-sre: Agreed. Immediate triage plan: 1) Quiesce new node (mark drain) so we stop scheduling to eu2-node-44; 2) collect nv-hostengine logs + NVML diagnostics (nvidia-smi -q -d PERFORMANCE, nvml events); 3) run microbench reproduce: small prompt storm from canary job to reproduce latency; 4) consider temporary re-packing of MIG slices to balance (maintenance window).

jess-support: I've asked customer for permission to drain node and run a controlled canary. They approved drain but want minimal disruption.

sophie-eng-runtime: Running nvml event dump now. Found repeated "GPU_RESET" events on GPU2 between 08:12:14 and 08:12:28; driver v525. We've never seen this pattern associated with dedicated pool before (mostly on bursty cohost).

kevin-sre: If it's driver reset, it could cause the runtime to evict contexts which shows as 429s and warmup latency. Two angles: hardware-level (thermal/PCIe/NVLink) vs driver bug. Check GPU temp/fan logs.

sophie-eng-runtime: Temps look normal (~72C), fans ok. But NVLink retrain in dmesg suggests fabric flapping — maybe a noisy neighbor triggered heavy NVLink traffic causing retrain?

anya-ml: Another hypothesis: tiny prompt fanout increases kernel launch rate so scheduler stalls and shares L2 causing stalls on heavily used slice (GPU2). Look at cudaLaunch failure rates in metrics.

kevin-sre: For immediate mitigation we can: 1) drain eu2-node-44 from the dedicated pool and let autoscaler re-balance to healthier nodes; 2) impose a temporary per-tenant concurrency cap on lantern-prod-17 to reduce small-request churn until we fix packing.

jess-support: Customer accepted per-tenant concurrency cap (50 concurrent) for next 2 hours. Implementing now.

infra-bot: action: tenancy-limit set tenant=lantern-prod-17 concurrency=50 by jess-support at 08:41

kevin-sre: Next steps for postmortem: collect MIG partition map across all nodes in that pool, kernel-level nv-hostengine logs, NVLink counters, and a capture of runtime scheduling traces for the 08:00-08:30 window. Also check if any rolling driver updates were pushed recently.

sophie-eng-runtime: I'll collect and drop artifacts in the incident bucket. Quick note: eu2-node-44 shows fragmented packing (one 2g slice plus three 1g slices). Repacking to even 1g slices across nodes would reduce imbalance but requires maintenance.

anya-ml: Recommend an offline workload that simulates micro-bursts to benchmark packing configs. We should capture p95 delta for 1g-only vs mixed pack.

jess-support: Customer happy with temporary cap and drain. They're okay with a maintenance window tonight for repack if we recommend it.

kevin-sre: Great. I'll open an ops change for repack with Sophie and Platform. Thanks everyone. :thumbsup:

sophie-eng-runtime: Adding note to the ticket: suspected NVLink retrain causing MIG slice reset -> context evictions -> runtime warmups -> p95 spikes. Will attach logs.

jess-support: Closing slack thread, will keep updates in the support ticket and postmortem doc.
